title: Break The Spin Review · Nov 13
subtitle: Stories 2-5 from the morning picks email; all real images (AI off).

posts.theme: Trump aims Vance at blue-state fraud
posts.quote: Truth Social card quoting Trump's post verbatim.
posts.alt: Official portrait photo of Vice President JD Vance above a white Truth Social-style card showing President Trump's post: I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the massive corruption and crime taking place in Democrat run cities and states. Billions of dollars is being stolen each and every month.
posts.caption:
President Trump just pointed his vice president straight at the blue states.

In a Truth Social post, Trump said he asked JD Vance "to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States." He named Minnesota, California and Illinois and called them "poorly run, corrupt disasters."

His claim: "Billions of Dollars is being stolen each and every month," and "Our Budget could be quickly BALANCED with the correction of this large scale criminal activity."

Vance already chairs the administration's fraud task force, created by executive order in March, and Trump named him "fraud czar" back in April. What changed is the focus, and the urgency. Trump wants the money found and the budget balanced with it. In the same post Trump wrote, "We don't need a deal with Iran," a sign that Vance's attention is moving from foreign talks to fraud here at home.
posts.first:
A fair warning on the numbers: Trump gave no examples to back the billions-a-month figure, and the task force's own fraud totals are the administration's claims, not an independent audit. That is the bar this effort will have to clear.

But nobody needs convincing that blue-state fraud is real. Minnesota's Feeding Our Future case alone involved roughly $250 million in stolen child nutrition money, and federal prosecutors charged dozens of people.

If Vance spends the next two years following the money in Sacramento, Springfield and St. Paul, a lot of people are going to have explaining to do.

posts.theme: Alito: Congress can turn off the lights at SCOTUS
posts.quote: ALITO JUST WARNED THE NEW CONGRESS CAN "TURN OFF THE LIGHTS" AT THE SUPREME COURT.
posts.alt: Photo of the U.S. Supreme Court building at dusk, darkened, with a red-ringed circle inset of Justice Samuel Alito's official portrait. Bold text below reads: Alito just warned the new Congress can "turn off the lights" at the Supreme Court.
posts.caption:
Justice Samuel Alito just said out loud what a lot of people in Washington have been thinking.

Speaking at the Federalist Society's Antonin Scalia Memorial Dinner, Alito warned that Congress could "turn off the lights" at the Supreme Court by cutting its funding. The Constitution protects the justices' pay, but not the money for clerks, staff, security and the building itself.

He called the judiciary the least powerful branch and said it is "vulnerable" to Congress and the executive. He also said some lower-court judges "have gone far astray in abuse of their powers." Justices Elena Kagan and Amy Coney Barrett went to Capitol Hill over the summer to ask for more money for the courts and their security.

Alito did not mention the midterms. He did not have to. Democrats take control of Congress in January, and some of them have already floated court packing, term limits, new ethics rules, investigations of justices and holding back money to pressure the Court.
posts.first:
The founders built the judiciary to be independent of the political mood of the moment. Lifetime appointments and protected salaries exist for exactly that reason. Using the budget to squeeze the Court would be a way around both.

To be fair, Alito also said judges themselves can overstep and "they make mistakes." The Court is not above criticism.

But there is a difference between criticizing rulings and starving an institution until it rules your way. If that is where the new majority is headed, voters deserve to hear it said plainly before the first spending bill is written.

posts.theme: Nvidia's Huang resigns over suspected-spy affair
posts.quote: AMERICA'S CHIP KING JUST QUIT. THE AFFAIR THAT TOOK HIM DOWN? A SUSPECTED CHINESE SPY.
posts.alt: Two panels: a photo of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang speaking at Stanford on the left and the flag of the People's Republic of China on the right. Bold text below reads: America's chip king just quit. The affair that took him down? A suspected Chinese spy.
posts.caption:
The man who built the company powering America's AI boom is out. Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and ran it for more than three decades.

Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia after admitting to staff that he had been "unfaithful to his wife." The relationship at the center of the scandal is with a woman reported to be a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia's board accepted his resignation, announced in a regulatory filing, and CFO Colette Kress is now interim CEO. She will also stay on as chief financial officer while the board searches inside and outside the company for a permanent replacement.

This is not tabloid gossip. Nvidia makes the advanced AI chips the United States has fought to keep out of Beijing's hands. Export controls, smuggling cases and national security reviews have all centered on exactly this technology.

Huang has agreed to testify before Congress. Lawmakers want to know what she could have seen.
posts.first:
An important caution: no charges have been announced, and China has denied the spy allegation. The word that fits right now is suspected, and that is the word we are using.

But the questions Congress needs answered are obvious. What did she have access to? Who knew, and when? No one should pretend that is a small question. Did anything about Nvidia's chips, customers or China strategy cross that line?

For years Washington has treated Big Tech CEOs as untouchable national assets. If the most important chip executive in America could be this exposed, the security review should not stop with one man.

posts.theme: El-Sayed Quran oath; backs Van Hollen over Abrego Garcia trip
posts.quote: MICHIGAN'S NEW SENATOR WILL SWEAR IN ON A QURAN. HIS PICK TO LEAD SENATE DEMOCRATS? THE SENATOR WHO FLEW TO EL SALVADOR FOR ABREGO GARCIA.
posts.alt: Photo of Abdul El-Sayed testifying at a U.S. Senate committee hearing in 2024. Bold text below reads: Michigan's new senator will swear in on a Quran. His pick to lead Senate Democrats? The senator who flew to El Salvador for Abrego Garcia.
posts.caption:
Michigan's new senator is already telling America who he is.

Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed told NPR, "I will likely swear on a Quran," naming a copy once owned by Thomas Jefferson or a historic one at the University of Michigan. He also called it "a delicious irony" that Vice President JD Vance is constitutionally obligated to swear him in.

If he does, he would be the first U.S. senator known to take the ceremonial oath on a Quran. House members have done it since Keith Ellison used Jefferson's copy in 2007. The oath itself is his right. The more telling part of the interview is who El-Sayed wants running the Senate.

He is backing Sen. Chris Van Hollen to replace Chuck Schumer, and his reason was not a policy record. It was that Van Hollen flew to El Salvador to check on Kilmar Ábrego García. "That's what leadership is about," El-Sayed said.
posts.first:
Remember who Ábrego García is: the Salvadoran man the Trump administration deported, accused of MS-13 ties, and later brought back to face federal human smuggling charges. Van Hollen made him a cause. El-Sayed calls that leadership.

That is the new Democratic Senate class in its own words. Not the cost of groceries, not border security, but a deported man's welfare as the test of who should lead.

Swear on whatever book you like. The Constitution is the one that counts, and El-Sayed said so himself. The question is whose interests he plans to put first once he takes that oath.
